n: Baseline. Shown by the conquest reports below, which take each place from the Romans; no chronicle states the border as such.
Baseline, shown by the conquest reports. Tabaristan's mountain lords were only loosely under Persia: uncertain edge.

cite.q: تكانبت الفرس وأهل الري وقومس وأصبهان وهمذان

n: Persian hold on Makran is not stated in the passages read; the region's edge is a guess.

cite.q: فلم تزل أرمينية في أيدي الفرس حتى ظهر الإسلام

n: The same passage adds the Romans held parts; the frontier ran through it.
Frontier land of both empires; the line between them at each date is not given in the passages read.
Arab kings of al-Hira under Persia. The end of their line (Tabari vol. 2) still to be cited.

cite.q: استعمل اياس بن قبيصة الطائي على الحيرة
قد تجمع له من الروم وعاملة ولخم وجذام

n: The Arab clients of Rome on the Syrian edge. The phrase names the northern tribes with Rome; Ghassan's own range is drawn from its towns: uncertain edge.
Abyssinian rule until the Persian expedition. The year of that expedition is not fixed: the app's first event is 571, so the change is placed at 575 as an estimate.
Persian-backed rule over Yemen. Date estimated.

cite.q: وكانت أرض البحرين من مملكة الفرس

name: عمان (الأزد)
n: Whether Persia held the coast at this date is not stated in the passage read.
Pastures of the tribe, drawn from places named with it. Tribes moved and overlapped; these are soft areas, not borders.

cite.q: إلى هوزة بن علي الحنفي وأهل اليمامة

n: Kinda and Hadramawt; independent standing before Islam not cited yet.

cite.q: وكانت قريش هي التي نصبت لحرب رسول الله
وترك النخل والأرض في أيدي اليهود

n: Its northern edge at the First Cataract is drawn, not cited yet.
Its reach is not described in the chronicles read; the outline is a guess beyond the coast.

name: المدينة
n: The Hijra.

cite.q: هجرة الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم
ودخلت خزاعة في عقد رسول الله

n: Allied by the treaty, not governed.

cite.q: فدخلت بنو بكر في عقد قريش وعهدهم

n: Banu Bakr of Kinana, in Quraysh's pact. Kinana as a whole is wider than Bakr.
Land left with its people on terms.

cite.q: ففتحها رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عنوة

n: Taken after Khaybar; Tayma on terms.
Year 8 AH; al-Baladhuri also reports year 6 for one of the two envoys (p. 84). Its kings kept their rule.

cite.q: فأسلما وأسلم معهما جميع العرب هناك

n: Year 8 AH; another report says year 6 (p. 86).

cite.q: فتح مكة وفي هذه السنة وهي سنة ثمان
وقامت خزاعة فقالت ندخل في عهد محمد

n: Sulaym marched with the Muslims; the date they count as subject is an estimate.

name: الطائف

cite.q: أمر وفد ثقيف وإسلامها في شهر رمضان سنة تسع

n: NOT at the siege (630.2), which failed: Ramadan 9 AH.

cite.q: غزوة تبوك في رجب سنة تسع

n: Tabuk, Ayla, Adhruh, al-Jarba and Maqna on tribute. The sources' date, Rajab 9 AH, is about Oct 630; the app's event says 631.5 (conflict 1).

cite.q: خالد بن الوليد بن المغيرة المخزومي إلى أكيدر

name: نجران
n: On tribute, keeping its faith. Year not given in this passage.
Year of delegations, 9 AH. Allegiance through delegation, not administration.

cite.q: قدوم الأشعث بن قيس في وفد كندة
أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ولى زياد بن لبيد حضرموت

n: Delegations, each with its own page in the Sira (1313, 1314, 1322, 1333); parts of each tribe stayed out. Year for each is 9 or 10 AH.
Year of Badham's conversion is reported differently; see the uncertain list.
Parts of both came in before the Ridda; no single date.
Juhayna's early alliance is reported, not yet cited; the date is an estimate.
Delegation reported; not cited yet.
End of the Lakhmid line: Khusraw has al-Nu'man killed and rules al-Hira through a governor. Tabari: «shortly before Islam»; the year is estimated. Dhu Qar follows from it (Tabari vol. 2 p. 193).

cite.q: وجهه إلى بلاد الشام فدوخها حتى انتهى إلى أرض فلسطين

n: Persians hold Syria and Palestine, the setting of Surat al-Rum. The cross was sent in Khusraw's 24th regnal year, about 614. The map showed all this as Roman.

cite.q: فإنه سار حتى احتوى على مصر والإسكندرية وبلاد نوبة

n: Khusraw's 28th regnal year, about 618. Tabari also says Nubia; no other text read says so (conflict 7).
The Romans regain them after Khusraw's death. The reports give no date for each province: the withdrawal is estimated at 628-630.
